name_note: The GTDB genus matches the literature genus Moraxella; almost all human upper-airway literature concerns the single species Moraxella catarrhalis.

sentences.text: The best-studied member of this genus, Moraxella catarrhalis, is an exclusively human organism of the respiratory tract mucosa, formerly called Branhamella catarrhalis.
Colonisation of the upper respiratory tract is highly prevalent in infants and children but decreases substantially in adulthood.
In culture it resembles commensal Neisseria species and can therefore be overlooked in samples taken from the human respiratory tract.
Published studies associate it with sinusitis, otitis media, bronchitis, pneumonia and ocular infection, and report it causing 15 to 20 percent of acute otitis media episodes.
